psychotherapy is a form of treatment that has not been proven to be effective in the treatment of mental disorders, and that the psychotherapist has no scientific or empirical evidence on which to base the claim that psychotherapy is effective.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the therapeutic relationship and the words that pass between therapist and patient are the most important ingredients for the success of any psychotherapeutic intervention.
we have been able to show that the psychotherapeutic industry is not immune to the economic forces that drive other forms of health care.

the therapeutic relationship is a complex, multidimensional and dynamic phenomenon, which is not easily captured in words, but which is also not easily captured by the ‘economy’ of the therapeutic relationship.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the therapeutic economy has been around for a very long time, and it has been a long time since it was confined to the consulting room.

psychotherapists should be wary of the ‘money and gain’ that is inherent to the therapeutic economy, and should be mindful of the fact that their own ‘gain’ is often a reflection of their patients’ ‘loss’.
